# ElecMini

> Keep the Electron JS API contract, drop the bundled Chromium, and render with the system WebView (WebView2 / WKWebView / WebKitGTK). A low-cost migration path for existing Electron apps: business code keeps `require('electron')` while the runtime is a Rust host (tao + wry) plus a Node sidecar.

ElecMini is not an Electron fork. It is a compatibility layer that lets an existing Electron application run on the system WebView instead of shipping Chromium. The headline win: the installer is about 3x smaller (Electron ~274MB vs ElecMini Slim ~84MB, roughly one third the size) with faster cold start; the trade-off is a documented set of unsupported/degraded APIs.

## Key facts

- Package size: installer ~84 MB (Slim) vs Electron's ~274 MB — about 1/3 the size (~3x smaller). Bundled engine footprint alone is ~2.3 MB (npm tarball ~150 KB + Rust host ~1.9 MB) vs ~274 MB (~118x). System WebView is a shared OS dependency, not bundled.
- API surface: 100% of official `electron.d.ts` members are classified as native / mirrored / degraded.
- Verification: full CI 23/23, differential contract 42/42, Codec consistency 10/10.
- Platforms: Windows (WebView2), macOS (WKWebView), Linux (WebKitGTK).
- Known boundaries: no true `contextIsolation`; APIs requiring Chromium internals are unsupported or degraded.

- [Real-project migration examples](https://github.com/outman2008/elecmini/tree/main/migrate/full-app) — electron-api-demos full-UI adapter plus three real-project API probes.
- [CLI and examples](https://github.com/outman2008/elecmini/tree/main/examples/minimal) — minimal runnable app.

## When to use ElecMini

- You have an existing Electron app and want a smaller, faster distribution without a full rewrite.
- Your app's Electron API usage falls in the native/mirrored tiers, or you can accept documented degradations.
- You can rely on a supported system WebView being present on target machines (L0 gate).

## When NOT to use ElecMini

- You are building a new app from scratch — prefer Tauri (Rust main process) or Electron directly.
- Your app depends on Chromium-internal APIs, true `contextIsolation`, or memory parity with Electron.
- You cannot guarantee system WebView availability on target machines.
